problem: A plural subject + are + singular noun is grammatical in general (Our employees are our greatest asset); the rule as stated is false.
fix: 文法錯：are 後不接原形動詞；當名詞「員工是興趣」也不通

problem: 'however' is also defensible: '...out of toner; however, the sales report will be printed tomorrow morning' reads naturally as reassurance (it will still get printed); add 'instead of today' to the sentence so only the cause-effect reading works.
fix: 分號後＋逗號 → 副詞連接詞；沒碳粉→改明天印（因果）→ therefore

problem: 'to Mr. Ito or myself' is very common in American business English and many natives accept it, so 'myself' is a risky second answer; replace that option with 'mine' to remove the ambiguity.
fix: 介系詞 to 的受詞 → 受格；拿掉 Mr. Ito or 再聽：send to me

problem: 'not A nor B' does occur in English (e.g., not for money nor for fame), so 'there is no such pattern' overstates; the real problem is that sentence-initial Not cannot start this subject.
fix: 文法錯：句首 Not 不能帶出 A nor B 當主詞；nor 要配 neither
